{{Quote|What the?!|Magaloof|<ref name="aotc" />}}
'''Magaloof''' was a [[Leffingite/Legends|Leffingite]]  [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Homeworld/Legends|from]] the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Almak/Legends|Almak]] who journeyed to [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] to pursue a career in the line of theft. Stealing an [[Airspeeder/Legends|airspeeder]] to get his break, he soon joined the gang of [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lord]] [[Hat Lo/Legends|Hat Lo]]. While in Lo's company, however, he sought to fall in with more significant syndicates, such as [[Black Sun/Legends|Black Sun]], or the [[Baath brothers/Legends|Baath brothers]]. In time, he entered into what he thought was a partnership with the [[Con artist/Legends|con man]] [[Achk Med-Beq/Legends|Achk Med-Beq]]. Together, they participated in several successful heists. However, Med-Beq and his partner [[Dannl Faytonni/Legends|Dannl Faytonni]] set up Magaloof while the Leffingite robbed a [[CoCo Town/Legends|CoCo Town]] [[Unidentified jewelry store|jewelry store]] of its [[flame gem]]s.

Magaloof was conned out of his take on the job, and became disillusioned as a result. He went to [[Prison/Legends|jail]] for the offense, and thought upon his folly. After completing his three-[[Standard year|year]] sentence, he returned to Almak to rethink his life. Magaloof had been eager to rise in the ranks of the underworld, and certainly hoped to make his mark amongst the criminals of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. He was ignorant of Med-Beq's con, and thought of him as a mentor, but, in retrospect, was disgusted by what had transpired, and had no qualms about dropping his intended lifestyle in favor of a more honest living.

==Biography==
===Early life and working for Hat Lo===
[[File:Coruscant-EotE.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Magaloof traveled to Coruscant (pictured) to pursue a criminal career]]
A [[Leffingite/Legends|Leffingite]] [[Gender/Legends|male]], Magaloof was raised on the [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of his [[Species/Legends|species]], [[Almak/Legends|Almak]]. At some point, he journeyed to the [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] [[Capital/Legends|capital]] [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], where he hoped to pursue a criminal career.<ref name="db1" /> Magaloof made his start by stealing a [[Gaba-18 airspeeder]], although this first theft nearly went awry<ref name="aotc" /> in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]]<ref name="Date">The events of [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II Attack of the Clones]], including when Magaloof nearly crashed with Kenobi, are dated to [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]] by ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> when the [[Droid/Legends|droid]] [[ASN-121/Legends|ASN-121]], with the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] in tow, shot past in close proximity. Offering only a loudly uttered desire for edification, Magaloof emerged unscathed, but shaken.<ref name="aotc" /> He offered the speeder to an associate of [[Hat Lo/Legends|Hat Lo]], a local [[Crime lord/Legends|crime boss]], who in turn offered him a position in his gang. However, Magaloof sought to reach loftier heights, seeking positions in better known syndicates, such as that of the [[Baath brothers/Legends|Baath brothers]], or even [[Black Sun/Legends|Black Sun]], an organization that spanned the known galaxy.<ref name="db1" />

===Partnership with Achk Med-Beq===
[[File:Achkmedbeq-Databank.png|thumb|left|200px|Magaloof worked with Achk Med-Beq (pictured).]]
Soon enough, Magaloof found himself in partnership with [[Achk Med-Beq/Legends|Achk Med-Beq]], a [[Coruscanti/Legends|Coruscanti]] con man. Eventually, due to his greater experience, Med-Beq became a mentor to Magaloof, teaching him the ways of the industry. The partnership proved to be successful, and a variety of heists were pulled off without a hitch. However, Med-Beq saw an opportunity to set Magaloof up, and took it. Convincing the young Leffingite to burgle a [[CoCo Town/Legends|CoCo Town]] [[Unidentified jewelry store|jewelry store]] and steal some precious [[flame gem]]s, Med-Beq enlisted his friend, [[Dannl Faytonni/Legends|Dannl Faytonni]], to masquerade as a [[Republic Security Force/Legends|Republic Security Force]] officer and confiscate Magaloof's flame gems following the robbery. Sure enough, Magaloof was "arrested" but let off with a "strong warning."<ref name="db1" />

Seeking to tell Med-Beq of the botched operation, Magaloof failed to find his mentor, and soon after, was arrested by the legitimate authorities for the robbery. Protesting his arrest, Magaloof informed the RSF officers that he had already been apprehended on the same charge, and that the missing flame gems had already been retrieved. The Leffingite was told that there was no "[[Lieutenant/Legends|Lieutenant]] Faytonni" in the RSF ranks and was sentenced to three years in the Moderate Security Ward of the [[CoCo Penitentiary]].<ref name="db1" />

Over the three [[Standard year|years]] of his sentence, Magaloof pondered his situation and came to the realization that Med-Beq had been setting him up from the very start. Disenchanted with the idea of being a criminal, and disgusted with himself for being conned so easily, Magaloof returned to his native Almak when released in order to restart his life and pursue a new career.<ref name="db1" />

==Personality and traits==
Magaloof was a male Leffingite that stood at 1.4 [[Meter/Legends|meters]] who was eager to please and excel as a criminal&mdash;his first robbery was a successful one, and he was able to pull off heists with Med-Beq for some time until he was betrayed. He lacked the experience required to recognize a con while in the middle of one, and in turn, suffered the consequences. He repented in [[Prison/Legends|prison]] and was not totally sold on the idea of being a criminal, which in turn led to his pursuit of a new life back home on Almak.<ref name="db1" /> The Leffingite had [[Color/Legends|blue]] eyes and orange skin.<ref name="aotc" />

==Equipment==
He wore a red [[shirt]] with a white collar during his time on Coruscant.<ref name="aotc" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Attack-Clones-Poster.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Magaloof first appeared in ''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones''.]]
Magaloof first appeared in the [[prequel trilogy]] film [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']],<ref name="aotc" /> which released on [[May 16]], [[2002]].<ref name="Year">''[[Star Wars Year By Year: A Visual History, Updated and Expanded Edition]]''</ref> In Episode II, the character was voiced by<ref name="Topps">{{Topps|set=2016 Topps Star Wars: Attack of the Clones 3D Widevision|cardname=Matthew Wood as Magaloof|link=https://www.ebay.com/itm/175187901844}}</ref> supervising sound editor<ref name="aotc" /> [[Matthew Wood]].<ref name="Topps" /> He was first named in an Episode II [[Depth Commentary]] available on [[StarWars.com]] that could be accessed through the DVD-ROM home release of ''Attack of the Clones''<ref name="Depth2">{{HomeVideoCite|film=2|featurette=Depth Commentary}}</ref> on [[November 12]], 2002.<ref name="DVD">{{SWArchive|url=episode-ii/news/2002/08/news20020801.html|text=Episode II On DVD & VHS}}</ref> 

Magaloof's backstory was later developed, when [[Gregory Walker]] wrote his [[Databank (original)|Databank]] entry, through the "[[What's The Story?]]" [[Hyperspace: The Official Star Wars Fan Club|''Star Wars'' Hyperspace]] feature on [[StarWars.com]].<ref name="db1" /> Normally, when writing "What's The Story?" submissions, Walker would start by fleshing out the character's story prior to their appearance in the given film. For Magaloof, he opted to begin with the character's scene, and work from there. He then mined the only other existing source on Magaloof,<ref name="blog" /> the [[2003]] [[Simon Beecroft]] and [[Curtis Saxton]] written reference book<ref name="Inside">''[[Inside the Worlds of Star Wars: Attack of the Clones]]''</ref> ''[[Inside the Worlds of Star Wars: Attack of the Clones]]'', for information.<ref name="blog" /> The final draft of the story was published<ref name="db1" /> on [[August 12]], [[2005]].<ref name="Round1">{{SWArchive|url=databank/updates/news20050812.html|text=Hyperspace Presents: What's the Story, Round 1}}</ref>

From his initial draft, he had his character cross paths with Achk Med-Beq, but the nature of the connection changed over subsequent drafts. Walker originally intended to have Magaloof aspire to join the gang of the character [[Volven Roxe]], from the 2003 [[Star Wars Roleplaying Game|''Star Wars Roleplaying Game'']] sourcebook ''[[Coruscant and the Core Worlds]]'', but this was changed to Black Sun during the editorial process. Also altered was Magaloof's prison sentence, which was intended to be four years rather than the [[canon]]ical three.<ref name="blog">{{Blog|narbflick|7|Magaloof: The Story Behind the Story}}</ref>

In creating the rest of Magaloof's story, Walker created such new elements as the species name "Leffingite," and the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] of Almak. He also made ties to the greater [[Star Wars Legends|Expanded Universe]], including CoCo Penitentiary from ''[[HoloNet News Vol. 531 56]]'' on the [[HoloNet News (original website)|HoloNet News]] website, flame gems from the [[Star Wars (1977) 99|ninety-ninth issue]] of the [[Star Wars comic books|comic series]] ''[[Star Wars (1977)|Star Wars]]'', and the Baath brothers from ''Inside the Worlds of Star Wars: Attack of the Clones'', who would become a fixture in Walker's later "What's The Story?" work for characters [[Acros-Krik]]<ref name="ak">{{DB|character|acros_krik|Acros-Krik}}</ref> and [[Nar Hida/Legends|Nar Hida]].<ref name="nh">{{DB|character|narhida|Hida, Nar}}</ref> Even though he had other winning submissions later in the program's run, Walker looked back on his Magaloof entry as his favorite.<ref name="blog" />
